Login takes the write lock before scrypt (src/app.mjs:49, src/handlers/session.mjs:29): an external writer got only 4 to 5 commits in 4 s. public/app.js:117 re-enables #login only after the body is parsed, and :109 treats an unparseable 401 on load as a plain 401 (both arguable readings). A version-0 file holding only sqlite_sequence is treated as new (classify at src/database.mjs:72 excludes sqlite_ tables), where A and C refuse it (ambiguous). Tests pass but are coarse: 49 broad tests; the two locked-database assertions (test/api.test.mjs:197, test/reports.test.mjs:118) check the message, not the time, and a grep found no test for ids above 2^53, unknown methods, CONNECT or parallel requests. The README is short (106 lines) and matches what I saw, except that 503 after 3 seconds did not hold on this Windows machine.

Z.notes: Ran: npm test (444/444 pass) and the same scratch probes: startup 55/55, API battery 233/234, extra edges 15/15, model routes 79/79, page script 61/61, and the stress run (503s in 3 of 7 heavy-writer runs). Ranked second: its test suite is the best and all green, but two behaviours fell short of A, one of them repeatably. Strengths: the same careful design as A: checks 3 to 7 in one transaction (src/app.mjs:62), a locked database retried on a timer (src/transaction.mjs:46-56) with 503 after 3.04-3.16 s and no delay for replies that need no database; BigInt reads with JSON.rawJSON output (src/reply.mjs:20), so ids above 2^53 stay exact; created_by requires an existing user (src/report-filters.mjs:81); unknown methods, CONNECT and Expect: bogus are answered by the normal checks (src/edge.mjs:163); the model path and query are sent byte for byte (src/model-url.mjs:36), attempts are limited on a monotonic clock (src/model-client.mjs:47-49), no transaction is open during the call, and session and ticket are re-checked before the audit write (src/routes/ai.mjs:55-56); a trigger failure gave 500 with rollback; stderr holds only error codes. The test suite is the strongest of the three: 444 passing tests including locked-database timing, raw-socket methods, chunked 413, rows changed by another tool, stand-in model timeouts and a fake-DOM page suite. Defects: every transaction starts with a plain BEGIN, writes included (src/transaction.mjs:29), so a write request reads first and upgrades its lock later; under a busy external writer (8 ms holds, 3 ms gaps) with logins in the mix, 17 to 19 of 120 write requests answered 503 after 3 s in 3 of 7 runs, and the slowest request in the clean runs took 2.3 to 3.3 s; A had no 503 in 7 of 7 runs (slowest 0.8 to 1.8 s). With a gentle writer, or without logins, C had no 503. The database was never held for anything near 3 s in these runs. src/edge.mjs:167 appears to write node's bare 400 at once for stray bytes after a Connection: close request, ahead of the reply still being prepared: a DELETE sent with an unframed body got 400 although the ticket was deleted (A answered 204; this needs a malformed client). public/index.html:105 adds width and height to #chart, beyond the element the spec writes out (no src, so probably harmless). package.json:8 asks for Node >=26, stricter than the >=24 of A and B. No CSP header on the page. The README (289 lines) is clear, and the parts I read (startup, routes, model contract, reports) match the behaviour I saw.
